look_here_first: Check for a thick woody root crown and persistent previous-year basal stems, then inspect phyllaries and rays.

morphology_keys.root: Woody perennial taproot and persistent basal stems
morphology_keys.head: About 24-65, occasionally 170, rays 4-7 mm (sometimes 11 mm); involucre 3-4.5 mm
morphology_keys.habit: Early growth may have one large head; late growth often many smaller heads

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. geiseri has a slender annual root and characteristic lower versus upper stem hairs; rays and flowering time overlap.
comparisons.cautions: Variable polyploid complex; voucher sometimes needed. E. plateauensis and E. lobatus var. warnockii are synonyms.

visual_comparison.annotation_policy: All targets have visible tissues in the pixels. No invented woody-crown, hair, or phyllary arrows; owner mobile arrow-tip signoff pending.

crew_field_sequence: Examine the rooted base: older woody crown and persistent basal stems are stronger clues than head color.
Inspect leaf shape and diminishing upper leaves; do not assign overlapping grass leaves in a photo to the fleabane.
Compare fresh rays, phyllaries, and fine hairs with E. geiseri using a lens and ruler.
A showy daisy-like head by itself cannot separate E. modestus from E. geiseri.
If roots are unavailable, record Erigeron sp. or a provisional comparison; preserve unresolved county native-range status.
